# Project rebaseline — proof → launch → reliability → control (2026-08-30)

This is the current execution authority for the open Verdify Platform backlog. It supersedes the sequencing in the 2026-08-29 point-in-time audit without erasing its evidence.

## Executive decision

Finish the already-built experiment path before broad platform hardening. Do not pull known maintenance, failed south/hydro hardware, platform-v2, twins, CNPG cutover, or control optimization onto the launch critical path.

The project now has six delivery waves:

1. **M8.1 recovery/proof:** complete #747, run current source-stamped readiness, execute the already-authorized Gate R, obtain the one attended Gate P decision, and seal one baseline → aggressive → baseline proof (#747, #749, #641, #750).
2. **M8 randomized day 1:** freeze one design, finalize exactly one internal draw, obtain the one separate launch decision, activate once, and carry the first exposure into the outcome/freezer path (#581, #587, #588, #639, #642; #640 follows the first completed assigned day).
3. **S1 delivery/runtime truth:** make delivery diagnosable and path-aware, replace VM-era tests, add real firmware compile/OTA gates, and close runtime/alert gaps.
4. **S2 durability/HA:** finish role-complete backup/restore and current-storage HA design before any CNPG cutover.
5. **S3 control safety:** simplify firmware and repair evidence contracts before expanding closed loops or tuning.
6. **S4/product and gated backlog:** auth work follows the core launch; physical, seasonal, twin, and platform-v2 work stays deferred until its real gate exists.

## Authoritative snapshot

Observed at approximately 2026-08-30 23:47Z:

- Source/default branch: `13e46c84e8531c2f7dfdd488c95d59d573a00d0e`; local checkout clean and equal to `origin/main`.
- `verdify-prod-dark`: `Healthy / OutOfSync` at that exact revision; last operation succeeded. Every core Deployment/StatefulSet is Ready, including API 2/2, MCP 2/2, ingestor 1/1, Hermes 1/1, planner 1/1, experiment workers 1/1, Lab 2/2, and DB 1/1.
- The sole writer and Lease are stable with zero pod restarts. The #433 launch-critical slice passed; its broader two-hour acceptance remains later work.
- Database schema is applied through migration 239. Migration 240 exists in source but is not live; the current pinned migrate image predates it.
- Experiment remains fail-closed: `draft / commissioning / emergency_hold`, component disabled, feature/vector off, no design lock, randomization, approval, proof receipt, outcome, export, reveal, or open exposure.
- The next scheduled backup is still required for #747: `lastScheduleTime=2026-08-30T08:17:00Z`; the successful corrected one-off is `lastSuccessfulTime=2026-08-30T11:03:24Z`.
- Latest eight climate rows have truthful north/west/east triplets, south absent, and a three-zone temperature spread of 3.42–3.60°F. That is below the fixed 4°F Gate-R limit that held the earlier run. This is a readiness opportunity, not a mutation or proof claim.
- South temperature/RH and hydro telemetry remain absent. Jason already classified those as nonblocking for this proof; #751 owns later repair.
- Planner graph runs remain 0; the trigger ledger has 2 unresolved rows and recent failures/timeouts. Routine Hermes/MCP delivery is healthy enough for the fast path, while broad recovery acceptance remains S1.
- Twin tables remain empty. Alert truth still includes 61 suppressed unresolved historical rows and 26 open alerts, including one critical component-integrity alert.
- The last Verdify CI Workflow is an infrastructure/error result at old revision `68cbacc4`; no later check exists. `main` has no required check/review gate. Common event/status/build/promotion work is owned by [jvallery/agents#4014](https://github.com/jvallery/agents/issues/4014); #644 owns only Verdify integration.

Known maintenance activity is deliberately outside this plan. Its observed effects are not re-diagnosed or used to widen project scope.

## Minimum-cycle delivery plan

### A. Unblock M8.1 with one actual image build

1. Take one fresh branch from current `main`. Adopt the exact known-good live API, MCP, ingestor, and ordinary experiment-worker digests into source so a full sync cannot roll them back; keep the readiness Job explicitly on its proven `66e0132…` image and current writer application-source binding.
2. Validate once. Build and consume only a new `verdify-migrate` digest. The readiness/orchestrator image build context is unchanged from its proven build and must not be rebuilt merely for manifest drift.
3. **Sync A:** reconcile the full application, unscoped and no-prune. Migration 240 runs PreSync; recovery readiness runs PostSync and emits the exact packet. No workload or writer rollout.
4. **Sync B:** bind that packet in a fresh already-authorized Gate-R activation, run only orphan recovery, and retain the no-exposure/no-proof-credit receipt.
5. **Sync C:** retire Gate R immediately and converge ordinary exact-pin source before any later sync.
6. Finish #747 on the next controller-owned scheduled backup.
7. After one fresh Gate P decision, **Sync D** activates the one attended direct proof and its required component-on writer rollout; **Sync E** retires proof authority and rolls the writer back to component-off after confirmed baseline.

The five operations are real data and safety boundaries, not process ceremony: Gate R needs a packet that does not yet exist, one-shot recovery authority must be retired, and the direct-proof contract requires explicit component-on and component-off writer transitions. Exact sequence and rollback contract: #750.

### B. Reuse the same runtime for randomized day 1

After the proof seals, do not rebuild the experiment runtime. In one coherent activation packet:

- freeze the future 60-day design and source identities;
- run one non-actuating OpenAI preflight;
- persist one immutable design lock and exactly one internal OS-CSPRNG draw;
- activate selector/lifecycle/freezer and the daily executor with feature/vector safety preserved;
- obtain the separate, exact #642 launch decision only after the locked artifacts exist;
- open the first exposure, retain rollback metadata, and carry the first complete assigned day into #640.

This leaves exactly two unavoidable human decisions on the critical path: Gate P and the post-lock randomized launch. Gate R is already authorized. All other `gate:jason`, physical, seasonal, CNPG-cutover, twin, and platform-v2 items remain outside the path.

### C. Stop paying for irrelevant builds

The smallest #644/#4014 integration slice should classify changed paths before image production:

- DB migration or orchestrator source: build only migrate/orchestrator.
- API/MCP/ingestor/planner/setpoint/publisher source: build only affected profiles.
- activation manifests, digest pins, tests, docs, and planning: validate, but build no images.
- generated digest-pin commits: do not recursively trigger builds.

Until the durable status producer is reliable, do not add a required-check/review gate that can deadlock delivery. Use one exact-head validation result plus exact Argo/live-image verification; enable branch protection only after the stable producer passes its reliability matrix. Planning and tracker updates stay in GitHub issues so they trigger zero repository builds.

### M8.1 — execute now (4)

body:
# M8.1 autonomous campaign: recover safely, execute Gate R, and seal one physical proof

This issue is the executable authority for the next campaign. It supersedes the older snapshot and wave text in this body while preserving prior comments as historical evidence. Project-wide sequencing remains in #775.

## Objective and exit state

Execute the smallest safe GitOps path that:

1. applies migration 240 and emits a fresh passing recovery-readiness packet;
2. executes the already-authorized migration-239 Gate R orphan recovery with no proof credit and zero exposure;
3. completes #747 on the next controller-owned scheduled backup;
4. obtains one fresh attended Gate P decision from Jason;
5. executes exactly one baseline-before → aggressive → baseline-after physical proof; and
6. returns production to `draft / shadow / closed / component-off`, feature off, active experiment ID empty, vector mode off, one writer, zero open exposure, exactly one sealed proof receipt, current backup, and exact-pin `Synced / Healthy` Argo.

The campaign ends there. It does not design, randomize, approve, activate, or run assigned day 1; those remain M8 work in #581/#587/#588/#639/#642/#640.

## Authoritative starting snapshot

Revalidated 2026-08-31 00:01–00:12Z:

- Repository `main` is clean, equals `origin/main`, and is `13e46c84e8531c2f7dfdd488c95d59d573a00d0e`.
- `verdify-prod-dark` is `Healthy / OutOfSync` at that revision; its last operation succeeded. The drifted runtime resources are the API, MCP, ingestor, three experiment workers, and two ingestor-image CronJobs, plus the currently active readiness hook objects.
- Core workloads are Ready. Live immutable image digests are:
  - API `sha256:3091ab604e8a22ae737d02518cd1f59eab662af81fe1c7d181226d1555b4d859`
  - MCP `sha256:349a0542b439defce625ff956020620f3a9bbecbae34e9f2ca42f8ef549bb7fe`

- The readiness Job deliberately uses `sha256:66e0132ba39c86d80f6fd74b442b376be004675262fbb03e48fbb486986617e9`. It was built from `d47541c6`; every Dockerfile-copied readiness/orchestrator input is unchanged between that revision and current `main`, so it is reusable. Do not rebuild it merely to change a manifest pin.
- The writer's latest 48/48 component-grid attestation still reports application source `bc8ad7d5fc6ec6330df8a9ab3a20ccd301aea3e4`. Keep that explicit application-source binding unless a fresh writer attestation proves it changed.
- Database schema is applied through migration 239. Migration `db/migrations/240-experiment-v2-readiness-reader-grants.sql` exists on `main` with SHA-256 `7fc9a584a7cdc3fc2b89c0bea18c1e3ec5fdd8c9e6261ccf3c2cb908320e7999` but is not live. All four intended migration-240 read grants are absent.

## Execution posture

## Non-negotiable safety boundaries

- ArgoCD is the only production deployer. Every production operation is the complete `verdify-prod-dark` application, no prune, no resource selector, from one exact Git revision.
- Before each sync, inspect the complete render/live diff. Do not apply unrelated desired drift. Reconcile source to the exact known-good live values needed to make the campaign diff truthful.

- Build only `verdify-migrate`. Rebuild another image only if fresh source proof shows its actual Docker build context changed after this snapshot; document that exception before building.
- Never edit migrations 225–239. Migration 240 is the only pending schema change in this campaign.
- Keep generalized vector mode off. Never create a second writer, randomization, assignment, design lock, outcome, export, reveal, or randomized exposure.
- Never delete or rewrite failed Jobs, attempts, authorizations, alerts, or ledger evidence to make a gate green. Never retry a failed proof attempt in place.
- Never expose secrets. Attach only redacted/secret-free packets, hashes, object identities, timestamps, revisions, and state summaries.

## Minimum operation budget

- Image builds: exactly one targeted `verdify-migrate` build.
- Pre-proof Argo operations: three complete no-prune syncs—readiness/migration, Gate R, then Gate-R retirement/ordinary-source convergence.
- Proof Argo operations: two complete no-prune syncs—Gate P activation, then proof retirement/component-off cleanup.
- Human decisions: one new Gate P decision. Gate R is already authorized.

These five syncs are data/safety boundaries, not ceremony: Gate R cannot bind a packet that does not yet exist; Gate R must be retired before later syncs; Gate P must first roll the singleton writer into its explicit attended authority and then roll it back to safe component-off state.

## Executable sequence

### 0. Rebaseline and prepare one exact release

1. Fetch current `main`; verify local/source SHA, GitHub issue state, Argo target/operation revision, full resource drift, live image IDs, singleton writer/Lease, backup status, migration ledger/grants, experiment axes, zero-state counts, and current climate quorum.
2. Verify again that the readiness image's Dockerfile-copied inputs have no diff from build source `d47541c6` and that the current writer's 48/48 attestation source matches the explicit application source. Reuse `66e0132…` when both hold.
3. In one source change, adopt the exact live API, MCP, ingestor, and ordinary experiment-worker digests listed above; retain the readiness Job's explicit `66e0132…` pin and active recovery-readiness binding; do not change any other workload template.
4. Run at least:
   - `uv run pytest -q tests/test_experiment_schema_migration.py tests/test_experiment_v2_readiness_reader_grants.py tests/test_experiment_v2_gate_r_readiness_activation.py tests/test_experiment_v2_proof_packet.py tests/test_experiment_v2_readiness_guard.py`
   - production kustomize render plus Kubernetes client dry-run;
   - `git diff --check`; and
   - a complete diff assertion that no pre-Gate-P writer/API/MCP/experiment-worker rollout remains.
5. Push the exact source revision and submit only the migrate image build:
   `python3 /Users/jason/repos/agents/control-plane/agent-fleet-control/runtime/agent-dev/agent_ci_build.py --repo-dir /Users/jason/repos/verdify-platform --revision <exact-pushed-sha> --image verdify-migrate --submit --wait`
6. Record the Workflow name, exact source SHA, resulting immutable digest, and successful terminal phase. Pin only that new migrate digest, validate the final release head again, merge it, and verify `main == origin/main` at the intended exact release revision.

### 1. Sync A — migration 240 plus recovery readiness

1. Start one full, unscoped, no-prune Argo operation at the exact release revision. Confirm its operation record contains no resource selector and no prune request.
2. Verify migration 240 applied and exactly the four intended read grants became true; confirm no new write grant.
3. Verify the readiness hook was recreated by `BeforeHookCreation`, completed successfully, and used readiness image `66e0132…` without rolling the singleton writer or other preserved workloads.
4. Retain the full secret-free readiness/guard output, packet SHA-256, derived exact Argo Git pin, application source, writer runtime reference, current generations, backup state, climate contributor proof, alerts, and zero-exposure state. Post the receipt to #749, #641, and #750.
5. If readiness fails, preserve the Job and evidence, keep production fail-closed, make only the smallest source correction, and repeat this phase only with a new activation marker. Do not advance to Gate R on partial evidence.

### 2. Sync B — already-authorized Gate R

1. From the exact passing packet, populate `deploy/k8s/activations/experiment-v2-gate-r` with fresh current IDs, axes, generations, writer reference, source identities, migration/recovery digests, packet SHA-256, and a fresh bounded window. Gate R is already authorized; do not ask Jason again.
2. Replace readiness in the canonical production overlay with the one-shot unsuspended Gate R activation. Render the complete production application and prove the only intended mutation is the recovery hook surface.
3. Merge the exact activation revision and run one complete no-prune, unscoped sync.
4. Require the Job to resolve only the retained migration-239 orphan, create no exposure, award no proof credit, preserve predecessor evidence, and finish feature-off/empty-ID/vector-off/component-off with zero exposure.
5. Retain the secret-free Gate R receipt and update #641/#750 immediately. Any mismatch remains a no-exposure hold and blocks the next phase.

### 3. Sync C — retire Gate R and converge ordinary source

1. Immediately remove the active Gate R component/values from ordinary production source; restore only dormant/absent one-shot surfaces.
2. Merge and perform one complete no-prune, unscoped sync so a later unrelated sync cannot replay Gate R.

title: #666 restore-rehearsal: migration 217 cannot re-own hostile TimescaleDB compressed-chunk owners
body:
## Context
Follow-up from the 2026-08-26 experiment-v2/Gate-2 delivery. The wave -2 `verdify-experiment-v2-restore-rehearsal` PreSync hook (added in #666) restores a real production backup and replays migration 217. Making it actually pass against real production data required a set of restore-path fixes (roles/memberships seed, matview refresh under pg_restore's hardened search_path, verdify-superuser bootstrap to match CNPG, `pg_restore --role verdify`, busybox-safe dump discovery, nss_wrapper for uid 999). Those are shipping with the delivery.

## The remaining gap (deferred here)
`db/migrations/tests/test-217-runtime-role-boundary.sql` is an adversarial fixture: it deliberately **poisons** object ownership, then re-applies 217 to prove re-normalization. Its poisoning reaches a TimescaleDB **compressed chunk** (`_timescaledb_internal.compress_hyper_*`), and migration 217's owner-normalization loop then attempts `ALTER TABLE <compressed_chunk> OWNER`, which PostgreSQL rejects (`operation not supported on chunk tables`).

- **Not a production risk:** production's live forward migrate applies 217 once against uniform `verdify` ownership; all internal chunks are datdba-owned (verified), so the loop never selects them. Only the fixture's adversarial re-application with poisoned ownership triggers it.
- For the delivery, the `test-217` fixture was made **advisory (non-blocking)** in the rehearsal hook; the core rehearsal (restore + first-apply migration + idempotency ledger + object/ACL preservation + test-214/216/218) remains blocking and passes.

## Fix options for this issue
1. In 217's exposed-owners loop + trust assertion, treat TimescaleDB-internal objects as extension-managed: skip direct re-ownership (they follow the parent hypertable) and verify via the hypertable rather than the chunk. (Correct, but touches #666's compressed-chunk assertion — needs review.)
2. Re-own compressed chunks via the supported TimescaleDB path (re-own the compressed hypertable so chunks follow), if such a path exists in TS 2.25.2.
3. Narrow the test-217 fixture's poisoning to owners that 217 can actually re-normalize.

Re-enable `test-217` as blocking in the rehearsal hook once fixed.

title: lab-publisher: surface S3 errors and classify cache-lock contention
body:
## Context

The publisher is currently healthy. A source and runtime review on 2026-08-30 confirmed two observability gaps, but disproved the stale-lock premise in the original issue.

## Verified current behavior

- scripts/s3-delta-sync.py captures AWS command output and raises on failure without emitting the captured diagnostic text. Upload and removal failures can therefore be opaque.
- The previous-manifest read treats every AWS failure as a cold start. A missing object is expected; authentication, endpoint, permission, and storage failures are not.
- scripts/lab-publish-k3s.sh uses a descriptor-scoped nonblocking operating-system flock and returns exit 75 on contention. That lock is released when its owning process exits; it cannot remain stale on disk.
- The CronJob already uses concurrencyPolicy Forbid and a bounded active deadline. Init containers and the CronJob are separate actors and can still contend on the shared cache lock during rollout or initialization.

## Remaining work

- [ ] On failed AWS operations, emit sanitized command context plus captured stdout and stderr without exposing credentials or secret values.
- [ ] Preserve the intentional missing-manifest cold-start path, while distinguishing object absence from authentication, endpoint, permission, and storage errors.
- [ ] Classify exit 75 as lock contention and provide enough holder or operation context to distinguish a normal concurrent init/publish from a stuck process.
- [ ] Add regression tests for failed upload, failed removal, missing versus inaccessible prior manifest, and concurrent init/publisher behavior.
- [ ] Keep concurrencyPolicy Forbid, the active deadline, and the existing active-lock safety contract.

## Safety constraint

Do not add a time-based lock breaker or remove an active flock. If a process is genuinely stuck, terminate the bounded owning workload and let the operating system release the descriptor.

This is reliability debt, not an active incident.

title: DR: production backups omit cluster-global roles/memberships (restore path incomplete)
body:
## Problem

Surfaced by the Gate-2 restored-DB rehearsal hook (verdify-platform#583 delivery). `pg_dump` of a single database carries **no cluster-level roles, role memberships, or the database owner**. A restore of a production backup into a fresh cluster therefore starts with none of the experiment/runtime roles, and any migration that asserts or normalizes role ownership/ACLs (214, 216, 217) fails closed against the restored copy.

The rehearsal hook (`deploy/k8s/components/experiment-v2-restore-rehearsal`) now compensates in-script by pre-seeding the exact role inventory + memberships and mirroring the DB owner before replaying candidate migrations. That makes the gate pass, but the underlying **backup artifact is still not self-sufficient for a real disaster recovery** — an operator restoring from `s3-hdd` today would hit the same wall.

## Fix

1. Add `pg_dumpall --globals-only` (roles + memberships + tablespaces, no data) to the `db-backup` CronJob, stored alongside each `verdify-*.dump`.
2. Document the restore order in the DR runbook: create cluster → apply globals → create db + set owner → `pg_restore` → migrations.
3. Consider having the rehearsal hook consume the real globals artifact instead of its in-script seed, so the gate proves the *actual* DR path end to end.

## Evidence
- Rehearsal iterations showed: `canonical v2 owner role is missing or elevated` (214/217), `collector login is not exact` (216), `permission denied for function` (fixture ACLs) — all traceable to absent globals.
- Non-blocking for the current e0be4e05 deploy (the live migrate hook runs against live prod, which has the roles); this is the standalone DR-completeness gap.

_Backlogged from the 2026-08-26 experiment-v2/Gate-2 delivery per operator decision._

Parent: #581. Inputs: #583 lifecycle/provenance, #588 frozen design, #639 observed fidelity/exposures. Launch integration: #642.

## Scope

Materialize the exact v2 daily causal dataset, same-study readiness evidence and safe one-way reveal. A deterministic SQL/CLI export is sufficient.

Pre-draw evidence remains on the study while lifecycle is draft but outside randomized assignment/ITT tables. Shadow emits immutable no-device `shadow_preview`; #641's scoped diagnostic uses `commissioning_probe`; after #641 combined signoff, moderate/aggressive canaries use `commissioning_canary` and A/A uses typed rehearsal work. Design lock closes readiness; locked/armed cannot reopen it. Historical v1 result bindings remain unchanged.

## Primary randomized ITT rows

Create **one row for every immutable assigned randomized local day** over that assignment's fixed local `[06:00,24:00)` window.

- Assignment/day/window determines row existence. Raw source availability determines endpoint value or null.
- Never select, filter, truncate or weight the primary row/window by confirmed-exposure membership or exposure coverage.
- Include known baseline fallback, failed delivery, rescue, manual override and zero-exposure days in their assigned arm.
- Irreducibly ambiguous treatment and missing outcome data remain in the ITT ledger. Apply the frozen null, physical best/worst bounds and inconclusive rule; never drop, reclassify, impute, shift or replace them.
- Confirmed-exposure union and the provisional `61,560/64,800` seconds measure treatment fidelity and define only a prespecified per-protocol sensitivity. They do not alter the primary assigned-day endpoint.

Emit blinded X/Y lineage: assignment/pair/date/fixed range, ITT status, expected/observed stable state, receipt/work lineage, exposure union/coverage/closures as fidelity, selector fallback, complete revision lineage, outcomes, safety/covariates and frozen sensitivities.

## Receipt and relational lineage

Use strict JCS/I-JSON with NFC rejection. Final schema hash is `db60b98661fb56dbdb9d3be6c987023db66fbacb638235c3f80a1a06160d5975`; canonical payload is `f0cdf57681748e9b2c2283162a0b9df22d3564ba2c97d95eecbefea22126dc6a`; receipt is `b3c1b6ca2b0c784206deaa0ac45b126f9a04793f7ac056ecd8761081d29f6875`.

The receipt embeds exactly firmware, config, registry and deployed-grid revisions. The wider source/image/profile/selector/sensor/corridor/outcome/analyzer/facility revision set is bound **relationally** through immutable study/work/bundle/readiness rows, not claimed as embedded.

Receipt schema enforces experiment/work/bundle IDs, phase and valid operation kind (`shadow_preview|commissioning_probe|commissioning_canary|aa_baseline_rehearsal|randomized_assignment|baseline_recovery` as applicable), exact 48-wire order and source epoch. Work references the matching preview/readiness/assignment/linked-recovery row. Generic typed-work expiry/mismatch applies in commissioning, A/A, randomized and recovery phases and closes exposure.

## Climate and localized safety

- Source-lock `public.climate` fields/resolvers and measured north/east/south/west T/VPD/RH.
- Floor to UTC half-open minute slots; average finite rows once; identical exact duplicates collapse; conflicting duplicates invalidate. No cross-minute tolerance/interpolation.
- A 15-minute bin needs at least 12 distinct slots. `e_i=max(L_i-x_i,0,x_i-U_i)` using the corridor at bucket start.
- Over the full assigned `[06:00,24:00)` window, compute the valid-bin weighted daily mean; null below 66/72 bins or with a continuous gap over 30 minutes. Missing bins affect raw availability/value, never row existence.
- Report worst measured wall zone only. House averages can be an approved center-screening proxy, never a center sensor. Air-dew screening uses Magnus dewpoint and air-temperature margin; bind manual crown/leaf checks, absolute limits, reference disagreement and missingness.
- Without commissioned center/canopy-surface/leaf-wetness sensors, make no true center/canopy/leaf condensation or crop-safety claim.

## Selected operating endpoint

Freeze one before draw:

1. commissioned variable operating cost using stream-specific resource evidence/uncertainty; vent uses travel events or motor energy, never vent-open duration; or
2. heterogeneous active/open-state minutes: eight relay-active streams plus `vent_open`, weight 1 each, for exactly `heat1,heat2,vent,fan1,fan2,fog,mister_south,mister_west,mister_center`.

`vent=true` is open state, not motor runtime. Relay/open minutes are not energy, water, cost, carbon or efficiency.

Each stream requires a direct initial state snapshot at or before 06:00 in local `[05:58:30,06:00:00]`, with no conflicting transition before 06:00. A post-06:00 or arbitrarily old seed is invalid. Integrate unambiguous state right-continuously over the fixed primary window.

For every device counter, take a fresh start sample in `[05:58:30,06:00:00]` and a fresh pre-midnight end sample in `[23:58:30,24:00:00)` in the same reset epoch. Reconcile the counter delta to the state-stream integral over **exactly `[start_sample_at,end_sample_at)`**, never flexible sample timestamps against the different fixed primary window. Reset/wrap/reboot needs separately fresh segment endpoints under the locked algorithm or invalidates reconciliation; a 24:00 post-reset sample is forbidden.

## Analysis and missingness

- Primary estimand is paired ITT physical admission of the AI recommendation versus frozen baseline under common virtual inference.
- For fixed `m`, `D_j=Y_AI,j-Y_Frozen,j`, `tau_hat=sum(D_j)/m`, SE `sample_sd(D_j)/sqrt(m)` with Bessel denominator, and the locked upper one-sided t bound.
- Advance only if safety/integrity passes, both climate upper bounds meet margins, and selected-benefit upper bound is below zero.
- The frozen design has 30 pairs and modeled joint advance power `0.13776` under Jason’s accepted-risk waiver; preserve and report it truthfully, with no later adaptation or power-qualified claim.
- Primary advance requires all locked pairs to have both endpoint values. Otherwise retain all assigned rows, report available-pair effects and frozen physical bounds, and classify inconclusive without imputation/replacement/denominator change.

## Readiness, roles and reveal

- #641 scoped approval precedes any `commissioning_probe`/#424/#433 write. #641 combined signoff separately precedes canaries/A/A. #642 separately approves randomized day 1 after lock/finalization and integrated evidence.
- Preview/readiness artifacts bind study, phase, kind, work ID, exact revisions, evidence window/pass state and expiry. Wrong/stale work, phase/kind/revision mismatch or arbitrary hash cannot satisfy a gate.
- Outcome freezer may read blinded assignment ID/X-Y label/phase lineage to build immutable X/Y exports, but cannot mutate assignments or read A/B mapping/secret.
- Blinded analyst is a distinct read-only role over frozen X/Y exports until reveal.
- Completion/reveal requires stopped admission, closed exposures, confirmed baseline or facility-owned emergency-safe closure, frozen outcome/deviation/fidelity/environment hashes and truthful integrity classification.
- Restricted one-way completion reveals once, reproduces schedule/mapping/commitment and runs frozen analyzer. Abort preserves blinded ITT and never reveals efficacy early.

## Acceptance

- [ ] One deterministic row exists for every randomized assignment's fixed `[06:00,24:00)` day, including fallback/rescue/failed/zero-exposure/null cases.
- [ ] Positive/negative fixtures prove confirmed exposure and `61,560/64,800` affect fidelity/per-protocol only, never primary row selection, window, weighting or truncation.
- [ ] Hand calculations cover climate slots/bins, missingness, all nine state semantics, exact at-or-before-06:00 seed, counter sample-to-sample interval/reset, selected endpoint and ITT bounds.
- [ ] Restored DB emits identical canonical rows/hashes twice and feeds the analyzer without reshaping.
- [ ] Final receipt schema/golden, valid phase/kind/work pairs, exact wire order, relational revision scope, typed-work expiry and anti-cache rules pass before lock.
- [ ] Draft probe/canary/A-A evidence stays outside ITT and cannot reopen after lock/arm; all three approvals are independently enforced.
- [ ] Fixed-m power/analyzer goldens and separate freezer/analyst/reveal role matrix pass.

## Claim discipline

No crop yield/quality, fertigation, MPC/PID, profitability or cross-greenhouse claim. Unselected endpoints and per-actuator runtime/cycles are secondary.

## M8 S0.1 reconciliation — 2026-08-29

- This issue is the post-start tail of M8, not a prelaunch blocker. Keep the milestone active through the first fixed [06:00,24:00) America/Denver assigned-day window.
- Close #640 only after exposure closes, baseline is safely restored, exactly one ITT row exists for every assigned-day disposition including null/zero-exposure/failure paths, the blinded outcome/export is frozen, deterministic replay produces identical hashes, and the analyzer consumes it without reshaping or reveal.
milestone: M8 — S0.1 Secure → Stable → Prove → Randomized Day 1

title: [P0][experiment-fast][L1/L2] Once-daily executor, verified component delivery and derived device truth
body:
Parent: #581. No dependency on #638. Use deployed setter/readback transport with generalized vector mode off.

## Target and work types

Build the sole once-daily component executor and an evidence-based exposure barrier around a sequential physical transport. Commands are not physically atomic; only confirmed full-state exposure is causal evidence. Ordinary planner/MCP/forecast proposals remain shadow-only.

Pre-draw work never masquerades as randomized assignment:

- shadow creates a phase-tagged no-device `shadow_preview` with no operation/outbox claim;
- #641 scoped approval permits `commissioning_probe`/#424/#433 work; only later #641 combined signoff permits `commissioning_canary` and A/A readiness operations;
- randomized execution uses an immutable assignment only after lock/finalization and separate #642 randomized-day-1 approval; and
- any baseline recovery first appends immutable `operation_kind=baseline_recovery` work linked to its triggering preview/readiness/assignment.

Locked/armed lifecycle is closed and cannot reopen readiness.

## Three resolver boundaries

The executor never privately resolves X/Y→A/B and cannot enumerate the schedule. It uses only the matching #583 `SECURITY DEFINER` resolver:

- readiness: experiment ID + readiness-operation ID + lease generation, unavailable in randomized phase;
- randomized: experiment ID + assignment ID + lease generation, unavailable to readiness work; or
- recovery: experiment ID + linked recovery-work ID + lease generation, admission must be `baseline_recovery`, returns **only** locked baseline and rejects assignment/readiness IDs.

Each reads `clock_timestamp()` exactly once internally after protocol/flag/lifecycle/phase/admission/time/lease/revision checks. Callers cannot supply time or read secret, mapping, raw arm, future assignments or bulk schedule.

## Physical boundary execution

1. Close prior exposure and verify writer lease/connection generation.
2. Resolve the one current typed work/target through its phase-appropriate resolver. The same frozen daily AI choice exists in both arms; invalid/late/unavailable remains baseline under ITT.
3. Converge through the locked baseline order.
4. Before any nonbaseline write, prove baseline using two qualifying ingestion-owned post-delivery complete 48-field epochs.
5. For a permitted nonbaseline target, send only differing allowlisted treatment fields as one exclusive, non-interleaved sequential bundle in fixed order. Prefixes are never exposure.
6. Persist truthful requested/queued/sent/failed/cancelled/superseded/confirmed state and immutable work/bundle/revision provenance.
7. Build complete observed state from cfg readbacks; open exposure only after two qualifying target receipts.
8. On ambiguity, close exposure first, revoke nonbaseline admission, retain randomized assignment in ITT when applicable, record deviation, then invoke only an authorized recovery path.

Six-hour exclusion is a preregistered analytical washout subject to power/carryover evidence. It does not make a prefix safe, establish carryover or qualify canaries.

## Exact state and receipt evidence

Stable `policy_state_content_sha256` uses exact domain/schema/full manifest digest plus the existing 178-byte `encode_policy_vector` and four locked state goldens. It has no observation time/generation.

`observation_receipt_sha256` separately uses strict RFC 8785 JCS over I-JSON with NFC rejection. Exact schema bytes hash is `db60b98661fb56dbdb9d3be6c987023db66fbacb638235c3f80a1a06160d5975`; adversarial canonical payload is `f0cdf57681748e9b2c2283162a0b9df22d3564ba2c97d95eecbefea22126dc6a`; expected receipt is `b3c1b6ca2b0c784206deaa0ac45b126f9a04793f7ac056ecd8761081d29f6875`.

The receipt schema enforces experiment/work/bundle IDs, phase and valid operation-kind pairing—including `commissioning_probe` distinct from canary—exact wire sequence 1–5 and 7–49, epoch/timestamps and bounded generations. It embeds exactly firmware/config/registry/deployed-grid revisions. Full source/image/profile/selector/sensor/corridor/outcome/analyzer/facility revisions bind relationally through immutable study/work/bundle/readiness rows. `work_id` references the exact preview/probe/canary/A-A/assignment/recovery row; invalid pairings cannot qualify or enter ITT.

Every baseline/target confirmation requires two receipts where:

- source epoch is generated/persisted by a distinct cfg-ingestion cycle after bundle completion;
- all 48 fields match expected stable hash and are complete, <=90 seconds old and <=60 seconds skew;
- writer/connection generations are current;
- epochs are at least 30 seconds apart; and
- every second component timestamp is strictly newer than the corresponding first.

Changing only epoch UUID/persistence time or rebuilding cached observations fails.

## Recovery, rescue and fences

- Treatment writes only approved differences among 11 fields. Initial enrollment, reboot/reset or common-field drift invokes recovery-only full-48 baseline under the same exclusive writer; all divergent fields, including common fields, restore in a separately replay-qualified order.
- Reboot/reset/reconnect/generation change closes exposure. After reconnect, linked recovery work restores/confirms baseline; never auto-reenter nonbaseline B that day.
- Manual/emergency override closes exposure, revokes nonbaseline authority and yields. Never send baseline until facility authorization says it is compatible with rescue.
- Without facility rescue ownership, automatic recovery is one bounded linked work item with current lease/connection; otherwise enter no-exposure hold and alert, never repeat writes.
- Every operation/lease/bundle/receipt/exposure is fenced by experiment, exact work ID/kind, protocol v2, phase, admission, server time, typed-work validity/expiry, relational frozen revisions and generations. Expiry/mismatch closes exposure and blocks claims in every physical phase.
- Normal close/disable/ordinary-writer handoff requires confirmed baseline; an immutable facility-owned emergency-safe-state may close authority without asserting baseline.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Generated contract proves one live setter/readback per treatment field and exact entity-grid/clamp validity.
- [ ] Preview/probe/canary/A-A/assignment/recovery work is disjoint and phase-tagged; draft/lock boundaries, all three approvals and cross-resolver/ITT rejection have negative tests.
- [ ] Resolver tests prove exact accepted IDs, one internal `clock_timestamp()`, recovery-baseline-only behavior and generic typed-work expiry/mismatch rejection in commissioning, A/A, randomized and recovery.
- [ ] Identical virtual AI inference exists in both arms; one permitted physical target per local day and no intraday admission.
- [ ] Exclusive bundles cannot interleave with dispatcher/MCP/forecast/retry/reconnect/operator writes.
- [ ] Baseline-first activation, target and rollback are restart/duplicate idempotent. Baseline itself needs two epochs before nonbaseline.
- [ ] Exact final receipt schema/golden, `commissioning_probe` phase/kind/work lineage, exact wire order, four embedded revisions versus relational full revisions, NFC/I-JSON bounds and anti-cache rules pass.
- [ ] Every treatment/recovery prefix from compiled defaults/observed starts passes replay before canaries.
- [ ] Fault tests cover partial/unknown delivery, stale work, wrong phase/kind/revision, duplicate/collision/lease loss, DB outage, reconnect/reboot/reset, cfg/common drift, cached receipts, rescue and interrupted recovery.
- [ ] Rollback is exposure-close/revoke → facility check → linked baseline/full-48 recovery → two epochs → lifecycle event → declarative disable/ID clear → ordinary writer restore.
- [ ] Restored-DB vertical test reaches #640 through the real setter schema; #433 runtime truth/non-starvation passes.
- [ ] Boundary shadow has zero calls; scoped-approved probe uses `commissioning_probe`; combined-approved canaries/A-A use readiness work; separately #642-approved randomized day uses assignments.

## Non-goals

New firmware/vector/hash/OTA (#586/#638), broader role split (#643), outcome analysis (#640).
milestone: M8 — S0.1 Secure → Stable → Prove → Randomized Day 1

title: [P2][platform-v2] Unify manifest/vector transport and firmware content identity
body:
Found by the 2026-08-23 resumption audit. ADR-0010 defers this generalized transport from the first confirmed-component experiment; it remains a real platform-v2 defect and must stay off.

## Problem

The merged host, SQL and firmware paths cannot execute one arbitrary policy vector:

- Host/ESPHome service arguments disagree: metadata vs `header_hex`, chunk `seq` vs `offset`, commit generation vs `slot/effective_at`, abort reason vs `slot`.
- Name-only availability checks report the unusable service surface as available.
- Firmware requires a committed experiment manifest; the host has no manifest encoder/sender/outbox stage.
- Python uses a domain-separated content identity, applied SQL requires raw SHA-256 of bytes, and firmware binds a different ROM revision context.
- Unit tests mock these seams rather than compiling/using the same interface.

## Acceptance

- [ ] One generated/shared definition governs service names/arguments, packed header, validity precision, treatment identity, slots, abort semantics and host call order.
- [ ] One canonical content/revision identity is implemented in Python, new ledgered SQL migrations and C++ with shared goldens. Already-applied migrations are never edited.
- [ ] Baseline/candidate templates insert into a migrated recent restore and real admission creates the intended outbox row.
- [ ] Host-produced manifest/vector passes compiled firmware commit, stage, validate, activate, expiry and abort paths.
- [ ] Periodic device receipt confirms manifest/content/activation/generation/assignment/validity/schema/firmware revision.
- [ ] Tests fail against the currently incompatible argument schemas and cover disconnect, unknown commit, identity rebind, reboot/power loss, expiry and ROM/approved-baseline recovery.
- [ ] HIL uses the actual generated ESPHome declaration, not a hand-written mock.
- [ ] Physical heap/recovery/OTA acceptance in #586 passes before any protocol enables this path.

## Fast-path boundary

#581/#642 keep `VERDIFY_POLICY_VECTOR_MODE=off` and use existing setters plus raw cfg-readback-derived exposure. Closing the fast experiment does not close this issue; closing this issue does not authorize switching the active trial transport.

Evidence: `docs/research/planner-experiment-resumption-audit-2026-08-23.md` §§4 P0-1/P0-2.

title: [P2][twin] Register verdify-twin image build profile in the control-plane contract
body:
The live twin still lacks a registered in-cluster build profile. ADR-0010 removes it from the confirmed-component experiment's physical-start critical path because that study changes no firmware and the present oracle covers only part of the promised policy/actuator surface.

This issue remains the precise platform/twin enablement task.

## Required control-plane change

In the owning `jvallery/agents` registry record (`registry/repos/gh-1247193937.yaml`), add the repository image profile:

```yaml
- name: verdify-twin
  dockerfile: twin/Dockerfile
  context: .
```

Regenerate the mirrored `.agent-fleet/ci.yaml`, build through in-cluster Kaniko to the Zot origin, verify the digest and pin the deployment source. GHCR and the pull-through cache are not push targets.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Owning control-plane contract includes the exact profile and generated repository mirror matches.
- [ ] `twin/Dockerfile` builds reproducibly through Kaniko, is verified in Zot and is pinned by digest.
- [ ] Runtime image requires no startup pip/gcc or unrestricted internet egress.
- [ ] Any deployment uses a read-only role, least-privilege network policy and a complete declared oracle scope.
- [ ] A twin result states exactly which policy fields/actuators are action-compared versus identity-only; partial coverage cannot claim full parity.

## Dependency status

Not a blocker for #642 or randomized experiment v2. It remains useful parallel evidence and a prerequisite only if a future protocol makes the new firmware/policy-vector platform its treatment transport.

title: [P0][experiment-fast][L2] Freeze selector identity, power-justified v2 design and randomization
body:
Parent: #581. Runtime/proof: #639/#641. Activation: #642 and draft #714.

## Scope

Freeze and verify the exact selector, design, randomization, and no-redraw identities for the accepted-risk direct study. This issue was reopened on 2026-08-28 because #677 delivered foundations but did not create the live design-lock/finalization receipts.

## Superseding decisions

- Provider/model: OpenAI `gpt-5.6-sol`, Chat Completions, medium reasoning, strict structured profile-only response, no tools.
- Context: deterministic last admitted row per 30-minute epoch bucket, at most 48 rows, with local request-size rejection persisted as `request_exceeds_context_budget`.
- Design: fixed 30 adjacent pairs / 60 local days.
- Modeled joint advance power: `0.13776`. Jason explicitly accepts this underpowered design; the waiver must be immutable and the study must not be described as >=80% power.
- No timed shadow or A/A prerequisite.
- Internal OS-CSPRNG finalization, exactly one draw, no caller-supplied secret, no redraw, and missed-start abort remain mandatory.

## Current truth

Source contracts are merged through #713, including #692 OpenAI wiring and #707 whitespace-tolerant Structured Outputs parsing. No experiment selector provider call, design-lock receipt, finalization/draw receipt, assignment, or exposure exists. Draft #714 is unmerged and stale at start date `2026-08-28`.

The physical proof failed safely before aggressive admission. A new design cannot lock until #641 has a sealed successful proof receipt. #686 must also be fixed before public activation.

## Acceptance

- [x] OpenAI provider request contract and frozen 30-minute context implemented.
- [x] One choice per study/local day, idempotent retry, bounded failure/fallback persistence, and treatment-blind inputs implemented.
- [x] 30-pair design and explicit `0.13776` risk waiver represented.
- [ ] New append-only physical proof attempt succeeds and its exact runtime/source/digest receipt is sealed.
- [ ] Real non-actuating production OpenAI preflight passes without DB/device/Kubernetes authority.
- [ ] Future start date is valid for the full 60-day America/Denver window and unused by any prior draw.
- [ ] Selector/source/runtime/analyzer/artifact identities and canonical design hash are recomputed from the exact qualified runtime.
- [ ] Immutable design lock is persisted.
- [ ] Finalization creates exactly one internal draw; duplicate/replacement/caller-supplied draw attempts fail without leaks.
- [ ] Day-1 schedule/commitment and no-redraw receipt reproduce byte-for-byte.
- [ ] Provider choice/fallback is persisted on day 1 and binds the expected frozen identity.

Close only after these database/runtime receipts exist. A green manifest or draft PR is not completion.

title: [P0][experiment-fast][L5] Coarse kill switch, v2 lifecycle and blinded integrity observability
body:
Parent: #581. Launch owner: #642. Contract: ADR-0010 and `docs/runbooks/experiment-rollout.md`.

## Scope

Deliver the minimal release/lifecycle/observability surface for the confirmed-component study while generalized `VERDIFY_POLICY_VECTOR_MODE=off`.

- Add a distinct safe-default coarse `VERDIFY_COMPONENT_EXPERIMENT_ENABLED=false|true` switch and one explicit stable v2 experiment ID.
- Do not encode `shadow|live` in the environment. Database lifecycle, execution phase and admission are authoritative: shadow is closed; commissioning/A/A/randomized admit only typed current operations.
- One source-aware hold gives only the bounded component executor authority over experiment-owned fields while ordinary planner/MCP/forecast proposals remain shadow-only.
- Expose authenticated, idempotent, optimistic-concurrency lifecycle/phase/admission and blinded-export API or audited CLI.
- Provide safety/integrity board and actionable alerts without comparative-efficacy peeking.
- Update declarative enable/disable, config-revision and exact-runtime probes. One image is released; bounded ConfigMap rollouts enable/rehearse-off/disable only the coarse switch. Phase changes do not restart pods.

## Required board/probes

Show generic `execution_phase`, `operation_kind`, `work_id`, validity/expiry and resolver/admission state for every preview/readiness/recovery/randomized path; stable expected/observed equality; receipt epoch/freshness/skew; 48-field completeness; activation/recovery/exposure; generations/reboot/foreign write; sensor/localized safety; manual/fallback; outcome completeness and rollback readiness. Show assignment ID and X/Y **only when operation_kind is randomized_assignment**; shadow, `commissioning_probe`, canary, A/A and recovery surfaces must not fabricate assignment/X-Y lineage.

Do not expose X/Y→A/B, randomization secret, comparative effects or unnecessary profile detail. Facility safety surfaces may show exact physical state.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Coarse switch defaults false, active ID defaults empty, vector mode stays off and feature-off behavior makes zero experiment device calls.
- [ ] One `kind=randomized`, `protocol_version=2` ID uses orthogonal lifecycle/phase/admission with template legal/cross-axis guards; v1 behavior is unchanged.
- [ ] Shadow/commissioning/A-A remain lifecycle draft: shadow has no-device preview work; #641 diagnostics are `commissioning_probe`; after #641 combined signoff canaries/A-A use typed readiness work outside assignment/ITT; design lock closes readiness and locked/armed cannot reopen it.
- [ ] Readiness, randomized and linked recovery-only resolvers expose only phase-appropriate current work; recovery returns baseline only. Receipt phase/kind/work lineage cannot cross those boundaries.
- [ ] Board/API uses generic phase/kind/work/expiry in all phases and exposes assignment ID/X-Y only for randomized work; expired/mismatched typed work alerts and closes exposure in every physical phase.
- [ ] Distinct approval state is visible/enforced: #641 scoped probe approval before `commissioning_probe` writes, #641 combined signoff before canaries/A/A, and a separate #642 approval before randomized day 1.
- [ ] `shadow` + closed admission runs at least 12 hours and through one complete scheduled cutoff/boundary/choice/state-hash/receipt/outcome-preview path (target 24 hours), with zero device calls/outbox leases and no ordinary-writer interference.
- [ ] Shadow→commissioning→`aa_rehearsal`→randomized uses audited DB transitions without ConfigMap changes/restarts; phase and full revision set are visible on every artifact.
- [ ] Enabled authority is source/field/phase scoped. `paused` denies nonbaseline work but permits authorized baseline recovery; `emergency_hold` denies experiment writes.
- [ ] Manual/emergency override immediately closes exposure, yields and alerts; no automatic baseline competes with rescue. Release from hold requires an immutable facility authorization event.
- [ ] A normal `closed` transition, completion, capability disable, active-ID clear or ordinary-writer restoration requires confirmed baseline. The only exception is an explicit immutable **facility-owned emergency-safe-state** closure event; UI/API must never relabel unconfirmed state as baseline.
- [ ] Stable state hash and observation receipt are displayed distinctly, use the exact v2 identities and are never called device-echoed.
- [ ] Alerts are fault-injected and actionable; visual polish is not a gate.
- [ ] Comparative efficacy/secret access is unavailable until #640 one-way reveal.
- [ ] Rollback proves exposure-close first, facility-aware recovery-only full-48 baseline when triggered, and two distinct ingestion-owned confirming epochs before normal disable/ID clear/ordinary ownership restoration.
- [ ] All config consumers carry the generated revision and exact expected revision/digests run after each bounded kill-switch rollout.
- [ ] Argo is Synced + Healthy without prune, exactly one writer remains, and public planner/data health stays green.

## Non-goals

- Production twin/build profile or long soak (#606).
- Generalized vector firmware/transport (#586/#638).
- Polished experiment-management UI or signed-result UX.
- Per-phase GitOps rollout/restart.

## M8 S0.1 reconciliation — 2026-08-29

- The accepted-risk fast path waives the 12/24-hour timed-shadow soak, commissioning canaries, and A/A rehearsal. Those checklist items are not M8 launch blockers.
- M8 still requires feature-off defaults, one stable writer, authenticated lifecycle control, actionable blinded phase/work/receipt/exposure/outcome state, distinct #641 and #642 authorization boundaries, immutable design/no-redraw enforcement, exposure-close-first rollback, full-48 recovery, and no mapping or comparative leakage.
milestone: M8 — S0.1 Secure → Stable → Prove → Randomized Day 1

title: [P2][platform-v2] Atomic firmware policy engine, ROM catalog, journal and recovery OTA
body:
Deferred from the fast experiment by ADR-0010. This remains a valuable generalized platform capability, but it is not a prerequisite for #642 and must not be enabled as a workaround for the current contract gaps.

## Scope

- Canonical generated 48-field schema and complete approved operational baseline/profile catalog in firmware. Registry defaults are not an acceptable experiment baseline.
- Immutable active/boundary/tactical slots and one-control-tick atomic activation.
- Heap-bounded manifest/vector or certified-profile service surface with one generated host/firmware interface contract.
- Complete identity receipt, expiry and assignment fencing.
- All 48 consumers read one per-tick policy snapshot; legacy setters cannot mutate armed fields.
- Two-copy crash-safe journal, corruption fallback, conservative reboot/water-budget semantics.
- Pinned experiment and recovery images built through approved Kaniko/Zot path, with source/toolchain/schema/baseline/binary identities.

## Acceptance

- [ ] #638's generated wire/content contract is resolved and shared by host, SQL and compiled firmware.
- [ ] Native, replay, HIL and power-loss tests cover every stage/commit/journal boundary, stale/duplicate/expired requests and both-copy corruption.
- [ ] Complete consumer-manifest drift tests remain green and no legacy armed mutation bypass exists.
- [ ] Physical heap/fragmentation and watchdog evidence meets a locked margin under worst-case telemetry/service load.
- [ ] Experiment and recovery artifacts are reproducible, digest-pinned and independently flash-tested.
- [ ] OTA scheduling receives explicit operator approval; staged rollout and at least 48 h device bake pass before this capability can become an experiment transport.

## Fast-path boundary

title: Alert-delivery contract: PrometheusRule CRs are inert here — rules load from the prometheus-rules ConfigMap
body:
## Problem

Multiple issues in this repo specify their alert deliverable as a `monitoring.coreos.com/v1` **PrometheusRule** object shipped into `deploy/k8s/overlays/prod`. In this estate that object is **inert**. Anything built that way will pass `kustomize build`, pass `promtool check rules`, reconcile green in ArgoCD — and never fire. That is the worst possible failure mode for an alert: a gate that has never been shown to fail.

## Probe (2026-08-02 ~14:15Z, read-only)

Prometheus loads its rules from a **ConfigMap**, not from the operator's CRs:

```
$ sudo k3s kubectl -n observability get deploy prometheus \
    -o jsonpath='{range .spec.template.spec.volumes[*]}{.name}={.configMap.name}{"\n"}{end}'
config=prometheus-config
rules=prometheus-rules
```

```
$ sudo k3s kubectl -n observability get cm prometheus-rules -o json | jq -r '.data|keys[]'
baseline.yml            cluster-quorum.yml      edge-synthetic.yml      hardware-health.yml
hardware-rollup.yml     homeassistant-energy.yml host-thermal.yml       k3s-node-pressure.yml
k8s-events.yml          longhorn-storage.yml    network-wan.yml         obs-restore-test.yml
pipeline-fabric.yml     slo-burn-rate.yml       verdify-backup.yml      zot-registry.yml
```

Meanwhile the CRD is installed but essentially unused — both existing CRs come from vendored charts, neither from a lane:

```
$ sudo k3s kubectl get prometheusrule -A
NAMESPACE         NAME                   AGE
cdi               prometheus-cdi-rules   60d
longhorn-system   longhorn-capacity      36d
```

The working example of how a Verdify alert actually gets delivered is `verdify-backup.yml` in that ConfigMap (`VerdifyDBBackupStale`, `VerdifyDBBackupExporterDown`) — verified live and used to close #395.

## Affected issues

- **#394** — "ship the VerdifyESP32SplitBrain/NoWriter PrometheusRule live". Re-scoped 2026-08-02; its `How` section prescribed a PrometheusRule CR.
- **#89** — "Device-route monitor in monitoring-ns Prometheus/Loki: blackbox TCP probe to :6053 + alert when ESTAB count != 1". Probe: `grep -rn 'estab' deploy/k8s --include='*.yaml'` returns **nothing** — still unbuilt, and would hit the same trap.
- Any future lane issue whose deliverable is phrased as "add a PrometheusRule".

`deploy/k8s/overlays/prod/writer-watchdog.yaml` records the history that produced this confusion: monitoring-stack was asked for a PrometheusRule on 2026-06-17 and never delivered one, so this repo shipped a CronJob watchdog instead.

## Ask

1. Record the alert-delivery contract for this repo in `docs/` (and ideally `AGENTS.md`): **Verdify alert rules are delivered as a rule file into the `prometheus-rules` ConfigMap in `observability` (monitoring-stack lane), following `verdify-backup.yml`. A `PrometheusRule` CR in this repo's overlays is inert — do not ship one.**
2. Add a guard so the mistake cannot recur silently: a test that fails if any file under `deploy/k8s/**` declares `kind: PrometheusRule`. Write the negative case first — add a fixture PrometheusRule, assert non-zero exit and assert the first error line — and include a positive control through the identical fixture plumbing plus a missing-path case, per the repo's gate standard.
3. Once (1) is written, restate #394 and #89 against it.

## Non-goals

Not proposing to change how the estate's Prometheus is deployed. If monitoring-stack later adopts the prometheus-operator and starts selecting `PrometheusRule` CRs, this contract gets revised — but until an operator is actually selecting them, shipping one is shipping a no-op.

## Problem

The current firmware does not match the actual greenhouse topology or approved crop-care intent:

- Climate wet-assist rotates center, south, and west; live today recorded center 16, south 8, and west 2 climate cycles.
- South/west time-window availability is treated as climate demand, so changing one eligibility flag is insufficient.
- Wall scheduled/manual fertilizer queues wall plus south and west fertilizer misters.
- Center drip and center/south/west fertilizer controls remain exposed; live center irrigation enable is on even though center drip is unconnected.
- Wall and center legacy schedules are daily at 10:30 while fertilizer admission ends at 09:00, so jobs are dropped accidentally rather than implementing policy.
- A global 90-minute post-feed hold blocks center climate mist despite fertilizer being wall-only.
- Climate and irrigation code can write the same relays without one ownership resolver.

Jason's approved intent is: center-only clean VPD mist; center mister is climate-only; automatic fertilizer on wall drips only; center drip and dormant south/west infrastructure are retained but disabled; both legacy 10:30 jobs are retired; weekly wall feed is a solar-cadence researched pilot using calibrated liters; missing commissioning fails closed.

One deterministic firmware resolver makes every command origin unambiguous. Center mist serves climate/VPD only. The wall-only automatic feed path is restart-safe, missed-window-safe, measurable, exact-once, and impossible to enable with guessed chemistry, flow, or duration.

- [ ] Every climate/VPD wet source resolves to center mist and produces zero south/west climate demand.
- [ ] Center mist accepts no irrigation, fertigation, manual-feed, planner-feed, retry-replay, or legacy-schedule origin.
- [ ] South/west clean irrigation requires explicit enabled intent and cannot race climate relay ownership.
- [ ] Center drip and dormant south/west irrigation remain represented but disabled by default with cfg readbacks.

- [ ] Both legacy 10:30 wall/center jobs are removed or ineligible; no fixed-clock 10:30 actuation remains.
- [ ] Weekly automatic admission uses solar/diurnal cadence, persisted exact-once eligibility, current commissioning revision, and explicit restart plus missed-window semantics without duplicate execution.
- [ ] Prewet, feed, and post-flush liters derive bounded durations only from positive current calibrated aggregate wall flow.
- [ ] Missing, stale, zero, non-finite, invalid, or out-of-bounds flow calibration prevents automatic feed.
- [ ] Sequence is clean prewet → feed → fertilizer off → immediate clean flush; the fixed 90-minute hold is removed.
- [ ] Missing/stale water chemistry, product analysis, injector ratio, distribution, volume, or flush endpoint prevents automatic fertilizer actuation.
- [ ] Tests cover every command source, reverse exclusivity, both 10:30 jobs, restart, missed window, duplicate trigger, cancellation, sequence order, liters boundaries, and all calibration rejection cases.
- [ ] Unit tests, invariants, replay, band replay, firmware compile/check, and `make irrigation-stack-software-check` pass.

- Adding sensors, plumbing, HAF, shade, or dehumidification equipment.
- Deleting dormant zone infrastructure permanently.
- Inventing one full-strength recipe for lime/citrus and cannabis.

Greenhouse firmware YAML/lib/tests, cfg readbacks and registry integration, irrigation job/feedback evidence, firmware FSM/design docs, and irrigation software audit.

title: Stop stable-connection full reconcile storms and make device writes truthful
body:
## Problem

Observed after PRs #431/#432 and ingestor digest `175e5ec`: ESP32 transport remained connected, but ordinary cfg readback changes triggered broad 69-value jobs mislabeled `reconnect reconcile` every roughly five to six minutes. Each job performed 56 anchor service writes and occupied the serial task loop for about 4m38s; one 300s timeout was visible. Each hour contained roughly 450–570 anchor pushes.

Verified causes:

- `_record_cfg_readback` reused one global force event for generic cfg drift and true reconnect; dynamic outdoor-dew-point readback repeatedly tripped it.
- All 56 staged registry anchor readback IDs differed from actual ESPHome wire slugs.
- Dispatcher cache/database state advanced before a paced batch physically completed, so cancellation could leave false sent/pending state.
- Sequential batches starved heartbeat, alerts, confirmation and planning work.

title: [EPIC] Firmware simplification: shrink on-chip surface to the irreducible control floor (heap/reliability root fix for #428)
body:
Full proposal: `docs/reviews/firmware-simplification-proposal-2026-07-06.md`. This is the **root fix** for the chronic-heap failure mode (#428); the #429 heap-guard is only the backstop.

## The data (first-principles: remove what the device doesn't need to own)
- **Tunable-sync : real-work traffic = 44 : 1.** The device's #1 activity by volume is confirming ~191 mostly-static tunables, not sensing/controlling.
- **DOWN:** 7,505 pushes/day, 87% from the band reconcile re-asserting ~101 params every ~5 min regardless of change; 88 params are pure CONSTANTS re-pushed 152,542×/60d.
- **UP:** `setpoint_snapshot` = **222,333 rows/day** (98% of all device output; ~40× the 1,405/day actual sensor telemetry); 100 of 191 readback params echo a constant value ~129K×/day.
- **Entities:** 612 total; **~400 (65%) are tunables + cfg readback echoes.**
- **Heap:** worst-case free 3–8 KB for weeks (vs healthy 38–44 KB) → the Task WDT panic.

## The tiers (each control-neutral → 0 replay divergence; independently reversible)
1. **Tier 1 (NO OTA, ingestor only, do first):** dispatcher pushes tunables ONLY on change (+1 re-sync on reconnect), not force-re-assert every 5 min. Kills ~85% of the 7,505/day + the constant echoes. Immediate heap/flash/network relief without touching the device. Band persists in NVS (restore_value:yes ×84) so this is safe.
2. **Tier 2 (OTA):** bake the 88 constant tunables → compile-time constants. Removes ~176 entities.
3. **Tier 3 (OTA):** collapse ~200 cfg_* readbacks → 1 config-hash. Removes ~200 sensor entities + the 222K rows/day.
4. **Tier 4 (OTA):** derive the diagnostic text_sensors (mode-reason, moisture-exchange JSON, candidate-summary, etc.) server-side via the byte-identical firmware-twin instead of publishing them.
5. **Tier 5 (OTA, optional):** batch the ~29 genuinely-dynamic params into one versioned config payload.

## Net (projected): 612→~150 entities; 7,505→~few-hundred pushes/day; heap floor 3.8→38-44 KB.
**Preserved:** autonomy (FSM+band+NVS unchanged), 72h network-isolation resilience, the AI control surface. **Improved:** heap headroom (no chronic WDT), flash-wear ↓40×, network churn ↓40×.

## Recommended next step
Start with **Tier 1** (ingestor delta-push PR, no device risk, reversible) and measure the heap floor for 3–5 days — it may lift the device out of the danger zone before any OTA, and reframes whether the #429 heap-guard OTA is even urgent.

Related: #428, #410, #424 (why drift detection matters), the 2026-06-17 control-story review (mechanical-floor tunables shouldn't be pushable).

title: Chronic ESP32 heap exhaustion (worst-case free 3-8 KB for weeks) → Task WDT panic 07-05; needs heap diet + controlled-restart safety net
body:
During the S8 flag-ON bake the device took a **Task Watchdog reset at 2026-07-05T15:44:56Z** (diagnostics.reset_reason='Task WDT', esp32_reboot info-alert 7510 auto-resolved).

**Why it's a regression, not background noise:** reset-reason history —
- pre-OTA 14 days: **10 resets, ALL 'Software reset'** (clean OTA/reboot), zero Task WDT
- post-OTA 2.6 days (binary ab18fe8): 1 Software reset (the OTA) + **1 Task WDT**

So the new binary produced the first task-watchdog hang in ≥2 weeks. A Task WDT means a loop task starved the watchdog past its timeout — candidate causes: the new per-cycle moisture-estimator work (held-temp gain + ladder adds float math every ~1s), a network/publish stall, or the added mx JSON emit. n=1, recovered, and the device has been stable 24.9h since — but it never happened on the prior binaries.

**Impact:** none on the climate outcome (flag stayed ON through the reset — readback continuous 1, no drying gap; the reset reverted nothing). But it is a real stability signal that **must block `firmware-promote-last-good`** (the rollback-floor promotion) until root-caused or shown to be a rare non-regression. Last-good stays on the pre-ab18fe8 floor meanwhile (safe).

**Asks:** (1) instrument which task starved the WDT (loop timing / task stack traces in the next crash); (2) check whether the estimator's per-cycle cost grew materially vs baseline (replay is offline so it won't show WDT); (3) decide a watch period (e.g. 7 days / N clean days) before promoting ab18fe8 to last-good. Corrects the S8 bake-report line that inferred '60h uptime, 1 clean reset' — actual = 2 resets, second was this crash.

Refs #410; diagnostics reset history + alert 7510.

title: Restore active Hermes/MCP planner delivery and truthful runtime health
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> Scope reconciled on 2026-07-09.
>
> The operational planner accepted by this issue is the ingestor → Hermes/GPT-5.5 → Verdify MCP path. The already-deployed planner_graph workload has zero production runs and remains non-authoritative. This issue may make that workload truthfully healthy or explicitly decommission it, but may not route production triggers/device writes through it or use it to satisfy required-plan acceptance.

## Problem

Required planner misses are a deterministic delivery-system failure class, not merely intermittent LLM hangs:

- Hermes can lose required Verdify MCP tools while Kubernetes/TCP probes remain green.
- Timeout rows often map to completed model sessions whose tool action never reached Verdify.
- Terminal status/result action is incomplete, allowing a run to age into timed_out or the wrong action to appear successful.
- Materialization can apply broader firmware bounds before stricter planner bounds.
- Plan rows lack durable validity/expiry and stale intent remains effective.
- Forecast scoring compares outdoor forecast with indoor observation.
- Critical alert 7676 remains open and blocks normal OTA.

A separate read-only finding showed both deployed planner_graph HTTP processes remained Ready after their planner-worker threads died on transient verdify-db DNS failure. Static health did not observe the worker. planner_graph_runs contained zero rows, so this is not evidence of the active Hermes failure, but the deployed workload cannot remain false green.

## Desired outcome

The active Hermes/MCP planner is tool-healthy, self-recovering, terminally observable, strictly bounded, and immediately active after acceptance. Every required trigger yields one valid expiring full plan or an explicit neutral fallback. The non-authoritative planner_graph workload is either worker-truthful and recoverable or absent from desired state.

## Active Hermes/MCP acceptance

- [ ] Readiness fails when required Verdify MCP tools are unusable.
- [ ] MCP deletion/restart and prolonged outage recover indefinitely with bounded backoff and no keepalive race.
- [ ] Every run persists terminal status/time, actual action, correlation, retries, and classified failure before SLA evaluation.
- [ ] A set_plan-required trigger is satisfied only by a valid full plan; one-shot/acknowledgement actions are distinct.
- [ ] Materialization intersects all bounds and normalizes once.
- [ ] Exactly one plan is effective; every plan has validity/expiry.
- [ ] Outdoor forecast is compared with observed outdoor temperature/RH-derived VPD.
- [ ] SUNRISE/SUNSET fault injection ends in a valid plan or explicit neutral fallback.
- [ ] Alert 7676 resolves only from a valid terminal required action.
- [ ] Planner becomes active after these checks; no proposal-only soak is required.

## Non-authoritative planner_graph acceptance

- [ ] Health/readiness observes worker-thread state and run-store reachability rather than static worker/db ok fields.
- [ ] Transient DNS/DB failure cannot silently kill the worker.
- [ ] Recovery uses bounded backoff or deliberate process exit for Kubernetes restart; no HTTP-green dead worker.
- [ ] Fault injection covers DNS failure, refusal, prolonged outage, recovery, and shutdown during backoff.
- [ ] A synthetic non-authoritative run reaches terminal state after recovery without producing a device write or satisfying a production trigger.
- [ ] Alternatively, reviewed desired state explicitly removes the unused workload.
- [ ] In either case, Hermes/MCP remains the production planner and planner_graph has no device-writer authority.

## Ownership

The planner-delivery lane narrowly owns planner_graph api/app/contracts/worker/store, targeted tests, and deploy/k8s/components/planner for health/recovery/decommissioning only. It also owns the Hermes/MCP delivery, ledger, materializer, forecast, schema, and context paths listed in its lane contract.

## Non-goals

- Moving deterministic five-second control or safety into AI.
- Making planner_graph the operational planner or a second writer.
- Treating a planner_graph synthetic run as SUNRISE/SUNSET acceptance.
- Bypassing firmware bounds.
- Clearing the critical alert manually.
- Retiring stale 0.25 intent before repaired consumers are live.

## Dependencies

#433 supplies fair writer cadence/canonical readbacks. #435 supplies unavailable-DLI semantics. #377 owns stale-intent retirement after deployment. #210 remains the separate legacy ingestor-local forecast_actions/MCP problem.

## Required release evidence

Exact service digests/revisions, tool-level readiness, required action terminal record, effective expiring plan, ingestor observation, alert resolution, and truthful planner_graph health/removal must all be tied to the deployed revision. No source-only result may claim production resolution.

title: [gate:jason][seasonal] Close the door screen-window when outdoor nights drop below the band floor (fall)
body:
## What
The door screen-window has been OPEN since ~2026-06-19 and **stays open until fall** (Jason decision 2026-07-03). This issue is the scheduled seasonal action + the tracking record for the envelope state.

## Why (verified 2026-07-03, 35-night prod data)
The window ~3×'d passive night air exchange: standing indoor−outdoor moisture surplus stepped **+5.7 → +1.9 g/m³** at ~06-19/20 with fog/mister source duty flat (~22%→~20%) and no heat1 night-duty increase (~22%→~17%). It is currently the dominant free night-drying actuator — it does passively what #410 builds actively. Its benefit inverts on cold nights (heat bleed, `vent_overcools` regime) and on outdoor-wet nights it imports moisture (the RH 80–84% nights of 06-21/24/25).

## Trigger / action
- **Close when outdoor nights regularly drop below the served night band floor** (roughly first frost-adjacent weeks; #410's estimator-gated vent+reheat path with its cold-night closed-heat fallback takes over then).
- Physical action = Jason (device-VLAN-adjacent but really just a window).

## Rules while open (binding for agents)
- **Never change the window state mid-bake/mid-experiment.** Every #410 bake / outcome_kpi comparison window must record the envelope config (window open/closed) — all #410/#411 baselines (+3.2 g/m³ "source", VPD 0.61 nights, ~0.83 achievable ceiling, measured slopes) assume OPEN.
- When it closes: expect the night moisture surplus to head back toward +5–6 g/m³; #410's active path (flag ON) is the replacement — re-baseline before/after.

Related: #410 (design review comment has the data), #411 (envelope is a third lever in that decision), #383.

title: Topology-aware cycling and runtime gate for every firmware OTA
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> Scope superseded on 2026-07-09.
>
> The blanket rule that every positive starts/day delta fails is retired. Weather, solar opportunity, and center-only topology make it invalid. The gate now uses transition-derived completed-day truth, issue-specific expectations, explicit tolerances, and insufficient_evidence.

## Problem

Firmware releases can regress relay cycling without failing units, replay, or compile; #295 is the historical example. The old proposal used partial counters and one rule for every relay. This recovery intentionally moves all climate mist demand to center, so topology-aware comparison is mandatory.

## Desired outcome

Every OTA is judged against matched, complete, provenance-bearing transition windows with explicit stop/rollback criteria.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Gate rejects current/future/overlapping/incomplete/incomparable windows.
- [ ] Artifacts record source/view version, window, timezone, code SHA, firmware versions, topology policy, completeness, and samples.
- [ ] Metrics include starts, runtime, short-cycle buckets, and peak transitions/hour per relay.
- [ ] South/west climate-attributed cycles are zero.
- [ ] Center compares with the prior combined center/south/west climate envelope.
- [ ] Other relays use explicit issue-specific tolerances/canaries.
- [ ] Verdicts are PASS, FAIL, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.
- [ ] Historical #295 fixture fails.
- [ ] Firmware preflight blocks last-good promotion on FAIL or insufficient required evidence.
- [ ] Unit fixtures cover invalid windows, metadata, topology, tolerances, and history.

## Non-goals

No firmware-counter truth, blanket zero-positive rule, partial/weather-incomparable comparison, old center-only baseline, post-hoc thresholds, or control behavior change from release tooling.

## Release evidence

Freeze baseline/policy before mutation. Use exact running firmware and matched complete post windows. A failed/insufficient gate blocks promotion; critical canary failure follows the predeclared rollback manifest.

- served-vs-pinched temp/VPD compliance;
- VPD high/low miss minutes and severity;
- feasibility/controller-attributable splits;
- actuator starts, runtime, cycle rate, and peak transitions/hour;

- DLI/DIF and solar-phase buckets;

Homepage/lab views should show the served crop corridor and outcome score. The target curve may remain visible as a reference, but it must not be the headline success criterion.
